title: Surcharge onto the surface and back
description: A storm hydrograph (peak 0.3 m³/s at 10 min, 180 m³ in all) enters a sewer whose outgoing pipe carries only about 0.06 m³/s. The manhole surcharges onto a 20 × 20 m walled hollow that falls 1 % towards it; when the storm passes, the water returns down the manhole. After three hours every drop has left by the outfall.

citations.title: The urban inundated area: a coupled 1D/2D model for the interaction between sewer and surface
Experimental calibration and validation of sewer/surface flow exchange equations in steady and unsteady flow conditions

expected_states.derivation: Everything that enters (the hydrograph's 180 m³) must leave by the outfall: the hollow drains to the manhole and the pipes drain freely.
The hollow slopes to the manhole, whose crest is at its lowest point, so no water can stay on the surface.

criteria.rationale: Outfall volume within 2 % of the 180 m³ that came in.
At most 1.8 m³ (1 % of the storm) left on the surface: a thin film on the 1 % slope drains slowly.

By the end of the run, the water stored on the surface and in the pipes has changed by exactly what came in minus what went out. A coupling that moves water between the two models must not make or lose any; each engine's own continuity error is allowed within this limit.

convergence.not_applicable: Scored on exact states that follow from conservation (exchanged and discharged volumes, settled levels): they do not depend on the grid.
